title: Batch the per-orphan get_closed_pnl backfill into ONE account-wide call per reconcile pass (no thread)
approach:
PROBLEM: in a single reconcile pass `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions` (and the cycle's `_reconcile_open_trades`) loops over every orphan trade and, for each, calls `_orphan_close_trade_row -> _orphan_close_pnl_backfill -> get_closed_pnl(symbol=symbol,...)` — one BLOCKING REST round-trip per orphan, executed inline on the WS consumer thread (via on_position_message -> reconcile_positions). A synchronized N-position close therefore fires N serial REST calls and stalls the sole reconcile authority for the full duration. The previously-rejected fix moved this onto a background thread — too risky on the single-threaded reconcile authority.

CORRECT FIX (single-threaded, O(N)->O(1), no thread): the Bybit client's `get_closed_pnl(symbol=None,...)` already returns ACCOUNT-WIDE closures with cursor pagination. So make ONE account-wide closed-PnL fetch BEFORE the orphan loop, group the records by symbol in memory, then match each orphan against its in-memory slice — instead of one REST call per orphan. Everything stays on the consumer thread; we trade N blocking round-trips for exactly one.

Mechanics (semantics-preserving):
1. Split `_orphan_close_pnl_backfill` into (a) a NEW pure matcher `_orphan_close_pnl_from_records(trade, *, now_ms, records)` containing the entire side/createdTime-filter + multi-leg-aggregation body (the part from `expected_close_side` onward — byte-for-byte the same logic, hence numerically identical) and (b) the existing `_orphan_close_pnl_backfill` kept as a THIN wrapper that fetches per-symbol then delegates to the matcher. Every legacy single-call caller (the ws_risk position_flat fallback at ws_risk.py:1905, and direct unit tests) is unchanged.
2. Add `_fetch_account_closed_pnl(trading_client, orphans)`: computes the fetch window as `start = None if any orphan has entry_ts_ms<=0 else min(entry_ts_ms-MS_PER_HOUR over orphans)` (the widest per-orphan window, so no closure is missed), makes ONE `get_closed_pnl(symbol=None, start_time_ms=start, limit=200)` call, and returns the records grouped into a `dict[symbol -> list]`. Returns `None` (not {}) when the endpoint is absent or the call raises, so the caller falls back to the legacy per-orphan path and nothing breaks.
3. Thread an optional `closed_pnl_by_symbol: dict[str,list]|None` param through `_orphan_close_trade_row` -> `_orphan_close_pnl_backfill`: when provided, the backfill SKIPS its REST call and matches `closed_pnl_by_symbol.get(symbol, [])` via the matcher; when None, the exact legacy per-symbol fetch runs. Default None everywhere keeps all existing callers byte-for-byte.
4. In BOTH `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions` and `_reconcile_open_trades`: first collect the orphan trades (those failing the keep-open check), then — only if there is >=1 orphan and the client exposes get_closed_pnl — call `_fetch_account_closed_pnl` ONCE and pass its result down to `_orphan_close_trade_row`. The per-trade matcher still re-applies the authoritative `created_ts >= entry_ts_ms` and `side == expected_close_side` filters in memory, so a single account-wide window yields IDENTICAL matches to N per-symbol windows.

Invariants preserved: require_evidence gating (the matcher still returns {} with no positive closure evidence -> _orphan_close_trade_row returns None -> trade kept OPEN), the C1 empty/error-snapshot guard (the `position_error` / empty-positions short-circuit runs BEFORE the loop and is untouched; a None batch result just degrades to per-orphan, never to close-on-absence), the exit_price/return/multi-leg backfill semantics (same matcher body), and the side-aware keep-open check. No on-disk schema change, no cross-sleeve config, no parameter touching a per-venue working dataset — this is a pure execution/infra refactor gated by numerical equivalence, so no pre-registration is required.

def _fetch_account_closed_pnl(
    trading_client: Any | None,
    orphans: list[dict[str, Any]],
) -> dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None:
    """reconcile-core-4: ONE account-wide closed-PnL fetch for a whole reconcile
    pass, grouped by symbol, replacing the per-orphan ``get_closed_pnl(symbol=...)``
    round-trips that stalled the single-threaded WS consumer on a synchronized
    multi-position close (N blocking REST calls inline -> 1).

    The fetch window is the WIDEST per-orphan window (``min(entry_ts_ms -
    MS_PER_HOUR)``; ``None`` if any orphan has a non-positive ``entry_ts_ms``, since
    that orphan's matcher applies no lower time bound) so no closure is missed.
    The authoritative per-trade filters (``created_ts >= entry_ts_ms`` and close
    side) are re-applied in-memory by ``_orphan_close_pnl_from_records``, so a
    single account-wide window yields IDENTICAL matches to N per-symbol windows.

    Returns ``None`` (NOT ``{}``) when the endpoint is absent or the call raises,
    so the caller degrades to the legacy per-orphan fetch path -- never to a
    close-on-absence. An empty account ({} = no closures) is a real, non-None
    result and correctly leaves require_evidence orphans OPEN.
    """
    if trading_client is None or not orphans:
        return None
    get_closed_pnl = getattr(trading_client, "get_closed_pnl", None)
    if not callable(get_closed_pnl):
        return None
    entry_times = [int(t.get("entry_ts_ms") or 0) for t in orphans]
    if any(ts <= 0 for ts in entry_times):
        start_time_ms: int | None = None
    else:
        start_time_ms = max(min(entry_times) - MS_PER_HOUR, 0)
    try:
        records = get_closed_pnl(symbol=None, start_time_ms=start_time_ms, limit=200)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - degrade to per-orphan fetch; never crash reconcile
        return None
    by_symbol: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    for record in records or []:
        sym = str(record.get("symbol") or "")
        if sym:
            by_symbol.setdefault(sym, []).append(record)
    return by_symbol


def _orphan_close_pnl_backfill(
    trade: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    now_ms: int,
    trading_client: Any | None,
    closed_pnl_records: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Query Bybit closed-PnL for an orphan trade and return backfill fields.

    Returns an empty dict on any failure -- the caller keeps the zero-PnL defaults.

    When ``None`` the legacy per-symbol ``get_closed_pnl`` fetch runs, so every
    pre-existing single-call caller is byte-for-byte unchanged.

    if closed_pnl_records is not None:
        return _orphan_close_pnl_from_records(trade, now_ms=now_ms, records=closed_pnl_records)

approach:
run_long_native_demo_cycle is a ~400-line monolith inside one exclusive_file_lock context. The pure sizing helper C (_compute_long_order_sizing) is already extracted. This completes the deferred work by pulling four CONTIGUOUS blocks into named helpers, each numerically/behaviorally identical to the inline code. This is a pure refactor gated by numerical equivalence (per AGENTS.md), not bit-identical output, and touches NO per-venue working dataset, NO live ledger on disk, NO cross-sleeve config — so it needs no pre-registration and no operator migration.

Sequencing (the right, no-shortcut order): land the CHARACTERIZATION HARNESS first, then the extractions. The harness (tests/test_liquidity_migration_long_native_cycle_harness.py) drives the REAL run_long_native_demo_cycle end-to-end offline: it monkeypatches only the data-acquisition seams in the module namespace (_demo_instruments, _resolve_ticker_snapshot, _build_long_universe, _download_recent_1h_klines, build_long_features), injects a fake market client + private_client=None, and feeds one live FC candidate so the candidate-selection, vol-target sizing, dry-run entry, ledger flush, cycle_row assembly, and persist paths all execute. It then snapshots the deterministic surface — the returned cycle_row (minus wall-clock timing_*/cycle_id), the payload structure, and the on-disk cycle/trade/order rows — and pins it as a golden. The harness exports run_long_cycle_snapshot(tmp_path, monkeypatch) so the snapshot can be diffed pre/post in one process; the committed golden makes any drift fail. I verified the harness passes against the CURRENT (un-refactored) tree, so it is a valid characterization.

- A) _resolve_cycle_inputs — public client + instruments/tickers/universe + empty-symbol RuntimeError + trading_client resolution + private snapshot unpack (equity/orders/positions/live-symbol sets).     ``date``-column derivation. Returns ``(klines, kline_cache_stats, features)``."""

def _persist_cycle_outputs(
    *,
    cycle_row: dict[str, Any],
    payload: dict[str, Any],
    cycle_now_ms: int,
    cycle_id: str,
    cycle_perf_start: float,
    root: Path,
    cycles_dataset: str,
    report_dir: Path,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """E-block: persist cycle telemetry + per-cycle report JSON/MD + prune.

    Identical write ORDER and timing semantics to the prior inline block: the
    report JSON is written BEFORE the final ``timing_persist_ms`` /
    ``cycle_elapsed_ms`` are stamped onto ``cycle_row`` (so the on-disk report
    omits them, exactly as before), then ``cycle_row`` is mutated in place and
    re-bound into ``payload['cycle']``. Returns the mutated ``cycle_row``."""
    # Persist cycle telemetry — matches the short sleeve's event_demo write path.
    # Without this the long sleeve has zero observability: no cycle history,
    # no skip diagnostics, no per-cycle equity tracking. Found 2026-05-24:
    # the reports/long-native-event-demo/ dir stayed empty for the entire
    # 11+h service runtime because the function returned the payload without
    # ever writing it. Partition by date to cap per-write cost like the short.
    cycle_date = datetime.fromtimestamp(cycle_now_ms / 1000, tz=UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    cycle_row_with_date = dict(cycle_row, date=cycle_date)
    persist_perf_start = time.perf_counter()
    write_dataset(
        pl.DataFrame([cycle_row_with_date], infer_schema_length=None),
        root, cycles_dataset, partition_by=("date",),
    )
    report_path = report_dir / f"long_native_cycle_{cycle_id}.json"
    report_path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=str), encoding="utf-8")
    (report_dir / "latest_long_native_cycle.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=str), encoding="utf-8"
    )
    (report_dir / "latest_long_native_cycle.md").write_text(
        format_long_demo_cycle_summary(payload), encoding="utf-8"
    )
    # Prune older per-cycle JSON to keep the report dir bounded — at ~1cycle/min
    # the snapshots would otherwise grow to half a million per year. Shares
    # the short sleeve's hourly-sentinel amortization so we don't stat
    # thousands of files every 60s.
    _prune_cycle_reports(
        report_dir, prefix="long_native_cycle_", keep_days=7, now_ms=cycle_now_ms,
    )
    cycle_row["timing_persist_ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - persist_perf_start) * 1000.0, 3)
    cycle_row["cycle_elapsed_ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - cycle_perf_start) * 1000.0, 3)
    payload["cycle"] = cycle_row
    return cycle_row

title: Rank live long universe by 90d-median turnover (match backtest): superset pool + lookback 100 + null-median fallback
approach: Backtest in_universe (long_native.py 652-660) ranks symbols by turnover_median_90d (min_samples=90), keeps top universe_size. Live _build_long_universe ranks by CURRENT turnover_24h and truncates to 50 BEFORE klines fetch (universe.py 100), so only 50 names reach build_long_features, universe_rank spans 1 to 50, the cutoff is trivially true and the median gate is neutered: membership decided by the wrong key. Top-50-by-median names past-50 by 24h are dropped; today-pump names (high 24h, low median) are pulled in where the median gate cannot reject them, and FC fires on those pumps. Naive re-rank fails: median needs 90 samples but lookback 90 gives ~89 daily bars after the end-trim plus hourly_bars at-least-20 filter, so null median zeroes the universe (deferral reason). FIX. A: widen _build_long_universe to a superset universe_superset_size 120 and let the existing median gate select the final 50 (no formula change; 24h floor + age filters stay). B: lookback_days + ws_klines_lookback_days 90 to 100, daemon _LONG_KLINE_UNIVERSE_SIZE 50 to 120 so the median populates and the store covers the superset. C: new helper _apply_median_universe_selection after _kline_window overwrites in_universe on the latest bar to the top-N by finite median (matching the backtest), backfilling by 24h only when fewer than N have a finite median, returning a 24h-fallback count threaded into cycle_row as universe_fallback_24h. test_code pins the body. Steady state means fallback 0 and a byte-for-byte match; cold-start uses the 24h fallback, no blackout. Selection-affecting so it needs pre-registration and is not safe now.

def _apply_median_universe_selection(
    features: pl.DataFrame, *, universe_size: int, snapshot_ts_ms: int
) -> tuple[pl.DataFrame, int]:
    # ls-4: set in_universe on the latest bar to top universe_size by 90d-median
    # turnover (matches the backtest). Backfill by 24h turnover only when fewer than
    # universe_size names have a finite median, so cold-start never zeroes the book.
    if features.is_empty() or "turnover_median_90d" not in features.columns:
        return features, 0
    latest_ts = features["ts_ms"].max()
    if latest_ts is None:
        return features, 0
    today = features.filter(pl.col("ts_ms") == latest_ts)
    if today.is_empty():
        return features, 0
    finite = today.filter(pl.col("turnover_median_90d").is_finite()).sort(
        ["turnover_median_90d", "symbol"], descending=[True, False]
    )
    members = set(finite.head(universe_size)["symbol"].to_list())
    fallback_count = 0
    if len(members) < universe_size and "turnover_quote" in today.columns:
        need = universe_size - len(members)
        cold = (
            today.filter(~pl.col("symbol").is_in(list(members)))
            .sort(["turnover_quote", "symbol"], descending=[True, False])
            .head(need)
        )
        fallback_count = cold.height
        members |= set(cold["symbol"].to_list())
    features = features.with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("ts_ms") == latest_ts)
        .then(pl.col("symbol").is_in(list(members)))
        .otherwise(pl.col("in_universe"))
        .alias("in_universe")
    )
    return features, fallback_count

Every write is a read-modify-rewrite of the whole file under the dataset lock (reconcile-ledger-5: O(history) write cost on the live hot path, where ws_risk submits stops), and ws_risk re-reads the FULL combined ledger on EVERY reconcile pass via `_read_combined` (quality-dup-5: O(history) read cost that grows unbounded for the daemon's lifetime).

FIX = month-bucket partitioning on a STABLE key, with a backward-compatible reader, a windowed reconcile read, and an operator migration of the live on-disk ledgers.

CRITICAL CORRECTNESS FINDING (the "confirm every writer's ts_ms stability" gate). Dedup in `_write_part` is per-part-file. If a row can change buckets across an update, the stale copy in the OLD bucket survives and `read_dataset`'s union returns BOTH copies — a phantom OPEN trade (`_open_trades` still sees the stale open row) on the shared netted account, which would corrupt the SOLE-reconcile-authority (ws_risk) state. So the partition key MUST be derived from a column that is immutable for the life of a row. I verified every writer:
  - TRADE rows: `ts_ms` is NOT stable — `event_demo_exits.py:665` (the execution-reconcile path) rewrites `"ts_ms": now_ms` on an UPDATE while preserving `entry_ts_ms` (=`opened_at_ms`, the original entry-order ts). `event_demo_entries.py:664`, `continuous_demo.py:951`, `long_native_event_demo.py` all set `entry_ts_ms` once at open; `record_tracked_exit_stream_fill` (ws_risk.py:837) and all `_upsert`/in-place updaters copy the existing row and never touch `entry_ts_ms`. => the immutable bucket source for trades is `entry_ts_ms`.
  - ORDER rows: keyed on `order_link_id`; `ts_ms` is set at creation (preflight `event_demo_exits.py:118`, `_continuous_*` order builders, long_native order builders) and the real order row that overwrites the preflight is written in the SAME cycle (same `now_ms`); ws_risk order updaters (`mark_order_filled_from_execution`, `mark_order_terminal_from_order_update`) mutate the in-memory dict in place and keep `ts_ms`. => `ts_ms` is a stable bucket source for orders.

DESIGN.
1) A per-dataset registry `LEDGER_BUCKET_SOURCE` in storage maps each month-bucketed ledger dataset to its stable timestamp column (trades -> `entry_ts_ms`, orders -> `ts_ms`). A `_ledger_month_expr` derives an int `yyyymm` (e.g. 202406) from that column via `pl.from_epoch(col, "ms").dt.strftime("%Y%m").cast(Int64)`.
2) `write_dataset`/`_write_dataset_unlocked`: for a registered ledger dataset, AUTOMATICALLY add the `_ledger_month` column and force `partition_by=("_ledger_month",)`, IGNORING the `partition_by=()` the caller passed. This is centralized so NO call site changes (every writer keeps calling `write_dataset(..., partition_by=())`). Rows missing/with null/zero stable ts fall into a `_ledger_month=0` bucket (legacy-safe; a malformed row never crashes the write). The on-disk layout becomes `event_demo_trades/_ledger_month=202406/part.parquet`.
3) `read_dataset_columns` (the single read path for these ledgers): after collect, transparently DROP the `_ledger_month` column so the returned frame is schema-identical to the legacy monolithic frame. The `glob('**/*.parquet')` already unions legacy `part.parquet` (at the dataset root) with the new `_ledger_month=*/part.parquet` buckets, so a half-migrated dataset reads correctly. Per-bucket dedup is preserved within each part; the SchemaError-fallback `pl.concat(how='diagonal_relaxed')` already coalesces differing schemas, and a final cross-bucket `.unique(subset=keys, keep='last')` (using `updated_at_ms` recency when present, mirroring `_write_part`) guarantees a `trade_id` that exists in BOTH a legacy part and a new bucket (the migration window) is never double-counted on read.
4) ws_risk windowed reconcile read: a `read_ledger_window(root, dataset, *, months_back)` reads only the most-recent N month buckets (+ the legacy monolith, which the migration drains) — sufficient because reconcile only needs OPEN trades and recently-touched orders, and a trade older than N months is either closed (irrelevant to reconcile) or, if still open, caught by the always-included legacy monolith until migrated. `_read_combined` uses the windowed read; bootstrap (cold start) keeps the full read so a restart re-loads all open trades regardless of age. Default `months_back=3` (hold horizon is days; 3 months is a wide safety margin).
5) Operator migration tool `scripts/migrate_ledger_buckets.py`: for each live ledger root+dataset, read the legacy `part.parquet`, split by `_ledger_month`, write each bucket via the new path (idempotent: re-running dedups by the dataset key), then atomically remove the now-drained legacy `part.parquet` ONLY after the buckets are written and a re-read row-count/`trade_id`-set check passes (dedup-safe: a `trade_id` present in both is unioned+deduped, never doubled). Migration runs on the PAUSED daemons (operator stops the 5 systemd services, migrates, restarts) so no writer races the migration.

WHY OPERATOR-GATED (safe_to_apply_now=FALSE): the code change is self-contained and numerically equivalence-preserving (read path returns identical frames), but the live VPS on-disk ledgers (`event_demo_*`, `long_native_*`, `continuous_fade_*` under the demo data root) must be migrated from monolith -> buckets while daemons are stopped, then daemons restarted. That is an on-disk migration of live ledgers an operator must run + own — it cannot be auto-applied by a push. The code is deploy-safe BEFORE migration (read unions legacy monolith; write starts emitting buckets), so the push can precede the migration; migration just drains the legacy file.

    # yyyymm as an int (e.g. 202406). 0 is the legacy/unknown bucket for rows
    # whose stable timestamp is missing/null/<=0 -- never crash a ledger write
    # on a malformed row; such a row still round-trips (read drops the col).
    if not ts_ms or int(ts_ms) <= 0:
        return 0
    import datetime as _dt

    d = _dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ts_ms) / 1000.0, tz=_dt.timezone.utc)

def _with_ledger_month(df: pl.DataFrame, dataset: str) -> pl.DataFrame:

    dataset, derived from its registered IMMUTABLE timestamp source. A no-op for
    datasets not in LEDGER_BUCKET_SOURCE or when the source column is absent."""
    src = LEDGER_BUCKET_SOURCE.get(dataset)

        return df

        pl.from_epoch(pl.col(src).cast(pl.Int64, strict=False), time_unit="ms")
        .dt.strftime("%Y%m")
        .cast(pl.Int64, strict=False)
        .fill_null(0)
        .alias(_LEDGER_MONTH_COL)
    )


def _recent_ledger_month_dirs(path: Path, months_back: int) -> list[Path]:
    """The most-recent ``months_back`` _ledger_month=* bucket dirs plus the
    legacy bucket (_ledger_month=0) -- the open-trade tail that has not been
    migrated yet. Used by the windowed reconcile read."""
    dirs = [p for p in path.glob(f"{_LEDGER_MONTH_COL}=*") if p.is_dir()]
    def _month_of(p: Path) -> int:
        try:
            return int(p.name.split("=", 1)[1])
        except (IndexError, ValueError):
            return 0
    nonzero = sorted((p for p in dirs if _month_of(p) > 0), key=_month_of)
    recent = nonzero[-months_back:] if months_back > 0 else nonzero
    legacy = [p for p in dirs if _month_of(p) == 0]
    return recent + legacy

row-count / key-set check passes.

from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl

from liquidity_migration import storage

    LEDGER_BUCKET_SOURCE,
    dataset_path,
    read_dataset,
    write_dataset,
)


def migrate_one(root: Path, dataset: str, *, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    path = dataset_path(root, dataset)
    legacy = path / "part.parquet"
    if not legacy.exists():
        print(f"  skip {dataset}: no legacy part.parquet")
        return
    before = read_dataset(root, dataset)  # unions legacy + any buckets, deduped
    legacy_df = pl.read_parquet(legacy)
    keys = [c for c in storage.DATASET_KEYS.get(dataset, ()) if c in legacy_df.columns]
    print(f"  {dataset}: legacy rows={legacy_df.height} key={keys}")
    if dry_run:
        return
    # Re-write the legacy rows through the bucketed writer (adds _ledger_month,
    # appends+dedups into the correct month buckets).
    write_dataset(legacy_df, root, dataset, partition_by=())
    after = read_dataset(root, dataset)
    # Safety: the deduped union must be unchanged in key-set and row-count.
    if keys:
        b = set(map(tuple, before.select(keys).iter_rows()))
        a = set(map(tuple, after.select(keys).iter_rows()))
        assert a == b, f"{dataset}: key-set changed by migration ({len(a)} vs {len(b)})"
    assert after.height == before.height, (
        f"{dataset}: row count changed {before.height}->{after.height}"
    )
    legacy.unlink()  # drained: buckets now hold everything
    print(f"  {dataset}: migrated OK, legacy removed (rows={after.height})")

                      "continuous_fade_paper_trades", "continuous_fade_paper_orders"]))

title: Account-wide margin budget + ws_risk-owned same-symbol reservation registry for the 3 netted sleeves
approach:
PROBLEM (two coupled cross-sleeve defects on ONE netted demo account run by THREE separate OS processes — short `event_demo`, long `long_native_event_demo`, continuous `continuous_demo` — plus the `ws_risk` reconcile daemon):

long-sleeve-5 (margin starvation): every sleeve sizes purely off `equity_usdt` (total account equity) with NO account-wide margin-headroom check. The long book is the worst offender: per-position notional = gross_exposure(1.0)/max_concurrent(10) × notional_multiplier(10) = 1.0 = 100%-of-equity notional per position, at entry_leverage=10 ⇒ 10% initial margin per position × 10 concurrent slots = 100% of account margin when fully loaded. The short (max_active≤12, lev 2) and continuous (max_active 25, lev 2) draw IM off the same wallet. A loaded long book can consume the whole margin budget so a sibling sleeve's `place_order` is rejected (or, worse on UNIFIED margin, raises the liquidation risk of the netted book). Nothing today bounds aggregate IM.

long-sleeve-6 (same-minute same-symbol race): cross-sleeve same-symbol exclusion is enforced ONLY via the venue snapshot `live_position_symbols = _active_position_by_symbol(raw_positions)` (Bybit REST/WS positions). Two processes that wake in the same 60s window both read "no live position on SYMBOL" before either fill lands, so both enter the same symbol — defeating the disjoint-sleeve invariant. There is NO shared in-process state because they are separate processes.

CORRECT DESIGN — make `ws_risk` (the sole reconcile authority, the only component that already reads ALL three roots) the OWNER of two pieces of shared cross-sleeve state, persisted in ONE new on-disk dataset that every sleeve cycle CONSULTS read-only before sizing/entering:

1. New dataset `cross_sleeve_account_state` (single-row-per-account control table, registered in storage.DATASETS + DATASET_KEYS). It carries, per account-key:
   - `account_im_used_pct`: aggregate initial-margin used across all three sleeves' OPEN trades (Σ initial_margin_usdt / equity_usdt), recomputed by ws_risk each reconcile pass from `state.all_trades` (which already concats all sleeves).
   - `margin_budget_pct_by_sleeve`: the pre-registered IM split (e.g. short 0.35, long 0.45, continuous 0.20 — operator-owned numbers, see pre-registration). This is the ceiling each sleeve may consume.
   - `reservations`: the same-symbol reservation registry — rows of (symbol, sleeve, trade_id, reserved_at_ms, ttl_ms). A sleeve about to submit an entry first WRITES a reservation (claim) on the symbol; sibling sleeves treat any active (non-expired, non-released) reservation on a symbol as an exclusion just like a live position. ws_risk RELEASES a reservation when the position is observed live (claim fulfilled → now covered by the venue snapshot) or when its TTL expires (claim abandoned → entry never landed). Because ws_risk already owns the per-symbol authority and runs continuously, it is the natural release authority; the sleeve only ever CREATES a reservation (cheap, append-only) and reads the registry.

   To avoid a NEW write-contention/race between three processes all writing the registry, reservations are modeled as an APPEND-ONLY claim log keyed on (symbol, sleeve, reserved_at_ms) — each sleeve only ever appends its own claims; ws_risk is the only writer that flips `status` to released/expired and is the only component that GC-prunes the log. A sleeve reads the log, folds it to the set of currently-active symbols, and excludes them. This keeps the writer model conflict-free (every process appends disjoint keys; one process — ws_risk — owns mutation of existing rows), consistent with the existing storage dedup-by-keys + `updated_at_ms` "freshest version wins" contract.

2. Margin budget consult: each sleeve, before its entry loop, reads `cross_sleeve_account_state`, computes its own headroom = min(its sleeve budget − its sleeve's current IM, total account IM ceiling − account_im_used). It SHRINKS its candidate list / per-position notional so the sleeve's planned entries plus already-used IM stay under both ceilings. The budget split sums ≤ 1.0 (with a safety reserve), so no sleeve can starve another. The long sleeve — the do-not-tune diversifier — keeps its signal/weights untouched; only the NUMBER of new entries it may open this cycle is bounded by headroom (book shrinks, never re-weights), preserving the diversifier's character.

3. ws_risk maintenance: in the existing rest_reconcile / reconcile pass, ws_risk (a) recomputes account_im_used_pct + per-sleeve IM from `state.all_trades`, (b) releases reservations whose symbol is now a confirmed live position OR whose TTL expired, (c) writes the updated control row + GC-prunes released/expired reservation rows beyond a retention grace. All under the existing per-dataset exclusive_file_lock; ws_risk is the single authority, so no cross-writer mutation race on existing rows.

WHY ws_risk owns it: it is already the SOLE reconcile authority, already reads all three roots (self.root + long_root + continuous_root), already routes per-sleeve writes, and already runs a continuous loop — it is the only place where "account-wide truth" exists. Putting the budget/reservation authority anywhere else would re-introduce the very split-brain this fixes.

This is a cross-sleeve architecture change touching all three deployed sleeve cycles + a new dataset on the live VPS, so the full design is FALSE for safe_to_apply_now. A strictly-shrinking, default-no-op SAFE SUBSET is carved out below (see patches[0] + the safe-subset note): a read-only account-IM headroom clamp in the LONG sleeve only, that reads the same new dataset but, when the dataset is absent/empty (the default on every current root), is a pure no-op — it can ONLY ever reduce the long book, never the short/continuous, never increases any size, and changes no number until the operator seeds the budget row. That subset is self-contained and numerically a no-op by default.

CROSS_SLEEVE_DATASET = "cross_sleeve_account_state"


def _long_margin_headroom_slots(
    *,
    root: Path,
    equity_usdt: float,
    order_notional_pct_equity: float,
    entry_leverage: float,
    account_key: str = "demo-unified-usdt",
) -> int | None:
    """SAFE, default-no-op account-wide IM clamp (long-sleeve-5).

    Reads the cross-sleeve control table written by ws_risk and returns the
    MAX number of NEW long entries this cycle may open without blowing the
    long sleeve's pre-registered initial-margin budget OR the account IM
    ceiling. Returns ``None`` (= no clamp, legacy behavior) whenever the
    table is absent/empty or unparseable -- so on every current root, where
    ws_risk has not yet seeded a budget row, this is a pure no-op. It can
    ONLY ever SHRINK the long book; it never re-weights and never enlarges.
    """
    try:
        ctrl = read_dataset(root, CROSS_SLEEVE_DATASET)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - control table is advisory; never crash the cycle
        return None
    if ctrl.is_empty() or "row_kind" not in ctrl.columns:
        return None
    budget = ctrl.filter(
        (pl.col("row_kind") == "budget") & (pl.col("account_key") == account_key)
    )
    if budget.is_empty():
        return None
    row = budget.sort("updated_at_ms", nulls_last=False).to_dicts()[-1]
    long_budget_pct = _float(row.get("long_budget_pct"))
    long_im_used_pct = _float(row.get("long_im_used_pct"))
    account_im_ceiling_pct = _float(row.get("account_im_ceiling_pct"))
    account_im_used_pct = _float(row.get("account_im_used_pct"))
    if long_budget_pct <= 0.0 or entry_leverage <= 0.0:
        return None
    per_pos_im_pct = order_notional_pct_equity / entry_leverage
    if per_pos_im_pct <= 0.0:
        return None
    sleeve_room_pct = max(long_budget_pct - long_im_used_pct, 0.0)
    account_room_pct = (
        max(account_im_ceiling_pct - account_im_used_pct, 0.0)
        if account_im_ceiling_pct > 0.0
        else sleeve_room_pct
    )
    room_pct = min(sleeve_room_pct, account_room_pct)
    return int(room_pct // per_pos_im_pct)
